title: What sets Soccer Stats Hub apart
subtitle: Transparent predictions, value versus the market, and a research workflow built for match day
dek: Soccer Stats Hub is for pre-match research. It's a published model with probabilities next to the bookmaker prices, BTTS and Over 2.5 tools and the filters you control. It's not in any way pretending to be a live score app.
authorLabel: Greg, founder of Soccer Stats Hub
intro: Football stats sites aren't all out to achieve the same thing. Some are all about chasing the live goals and pushing the alerts. Some have entire archives of every single career table you can imagine. Others are all about selling you tip sheets with absolutely nothing to check. Soccer Stats Hub is in a different camp entirely. It's all about pre-match research for the fan/bettor who wants to see the numbers behind the pick rather than just the pick.

That focus is absolutely everything on the site. The predictions come with a published methodology. The model probabilities are displayed alongside the bookmaker prices so you can see where they agree and where they disagree. BTTS, Over 2.5 and multi tools are all built around the way people actually go about shortlisting games. Premium gives you access to the full range at a price which is typically a lot less than you'd pay for a typical paid research and AI insights subscription. Here's what that actually means in practice.

sections.heading: A transparent model, not a black box
paragraphs: A tip without a reason is just a claim. On Soccer Stats Hub the path is clear. You build up a team picture from the fixtures that have already been played in the competition, convert attack and defence into expected goals for the match, then apply a Poisson scoreline grid with a Dixon-Coles style tweak for the low scoring games. From that grid you get the most likely scoreline, the home/draw/away percentages, the BTTS and the Over/Under 2.5.

We also publish that story properly. The methodology page and our article on how we predict a game walk through lambdas, form windows, missing player context and non-penalty xG. You don't have to reverse engineer a mystery percentage. You can read how the number was formed and then decide for yourself whether you trust it for that fixture.

sections.heading: Model probability next to the market
paragraphs: Research is not "the model said 2-1 so it must win". A better approach is to ask where the match history and the market agree and where they don't. If you expand a fixture you'll see the model's probabilities alongside the bookmaker implied prices for the main outcomes, with a value % when they differ.

That value layer is present in the daily board too: the best value picks, the insight rankings, and the filters which will only show you games with a minimum edge on match result, Over 2.5, or BTTS. Edge is not in itself a 'go' signal. Big gaps can be noise. The fact that you can put the disagreement on the page is one of the clearest distinctions between a research tool and a tipster screenshot.

sections.heading: A workflow for shortlisting, not scrolling forever
paragraphs: Stats dumps require you to open every match and re-type the same checklist from scratch. Soccer Stats Hub is all about the shortlist.

Customise Tips allows you to set your presets and sliders for value, form, probabilities and odds and then regenerate the tip list so only the games that match your criteria survive. There are dedicated BTTS and Over 2.5 research pages which will show you the teams and fixtures in those markets. Once the predictions have run you can then go on to build your own multis (including goals based and exotic cover multis) and copy them when you're ready.

You can also add fixtures to a shareable shortlist URL, capture charts as images, and go into the competition pages, which give you the league averages, standings, team rankings, and comparison charts. The whole idea is to have fewer tabs and more decisions that you can actually explain.

sections.heading: Match intel that goes deeper than the competition
paragraphs: Once a fixture is expanded, the useful question is rarely 'who wins'. Context is just as important: absences, how rested the sides are, recent patterns, and whether the market has already priced that in. All of that matters.

Premium match views include streaks across competitions, manager context, all upcoming fixtures side by side and missing player impact presented as attack and defensive contribution rather than a simple injury list. Form context covers rest days, congestion and schedule strength. AI match previews bring together the ratings, score ideas and key players in one easy to digest narrative when you want a bit of story to go with the charts.
None of that replaces actually watching the game. It will of course replace hunting around five different apps for scraps of the same story.

sections.heading: Coverage with season context, not only a feed
paragraphs: We cover roughly 50 competitions at any one time (from the Premier League and Champions League right down to the various leagues and cups that serious researchers actually use). We're far more selective than the global live score apps in terms of coverage. For us the depth of the prediction and the comparison is far more important than simply having a big coverage number.

We also have editorial hubs around the daily board where they're needed, i.e. a FIFA World Cup 2026 hub with the news, groups, team guides and key matches and a Premier League season preview with the storylines and market odds sourced. Those are alongside the model so big tournaments and season launches aren't just a fixture list.

sections.heading: Premium priced for research, not for a tipster markup
paragraphs: Core browsing and a bit of each day's fixtures is free so you can assess the product prior to paying. Free users see around a quarter of the board, the key stats and a limited tip view. Premium gives you access to every match across all the competitions we cover, full multi and market tip lists, the AI previews, the full insights and rankings and all the deeper match insight described above.

Paid research and AI insights subscriptions in this space are generally in the £10-£25 per month bracket. Soccer Stats Hub Premium is £4.99 per month or £39.99 for the year (other currencies available at checkout). In that same bracket, the monthly Premium is typically around half to four fifths of the price. The annual plan is usually 70% or more cheaper than the equivalent of paying the higher monthly rates for a full year.

We're not comparing ourselves to the free live score apps which essentially just offer ad removal. Those are a different proposition. We're talking about the paid layers that provide forecasts, filters and research depth. Payments are secure and go through Stripe. You can cancel at any time.

sections.heading: What we are not trying to be
paragraphs: Honesty is part of the product. Soccer Stats Hub is not a live score centre in any sense of the word. There is no live minute by minute feed and there is no push alert when a goal goes in. We are not some kind of career scouting archive with every single player table from every era and we don't pretend to have a proprietary event feed that no-one else can get their hands on. We take industry data sources and combine that with our own modelling, presentation and research.

If you want live second screen coverage then use a live score app. If you want the deep historical scouting tables then use an archive. If you want the transparent pre-match probabilities (value versus the market), BTTS, Over 2.5, all the filters you can think of and the like, that's the job we've built.

sections.heading: On the side of fans, not bookmakers
paragraphs: We actively avoid any form of affiliate marketing with bookmakers. Some of the deals out there are simply a flat fee paid when a customer signs up and deposits. A number of the others (particularly the revenue share type) are a cut of the operator's net gaming revenue from the customers you refer. That revenue is derived from stakes less winnings, less bonuses and less fees so the affiliate's income goes up as those customers lose more than they win. We'd rather not take a cut of that.

Soccer Stats Hub will show the prices so you can compare the model to the market. It won't be pushing you in any particular direction towards a bookmaker, nor will it be presenting a signup bonus as if it's any kind of recommendation. The odds are presented in the context of research. The product is firmly on the side of the fan who wants to understand the fixture rather than the side of the bookies.

sections.heading: How to use it responsibly
paragraphs: Predictions are models. The teams change shape overnight. Red cards happen. A clinical striker can miss an open goal. Treat every output as a research aid rather than a guarantee.

If you're using football stats for your betting research, please abide by local laws and only bet what you can afford to lose. We link to BeGambleAware for a reason. The whole point of Soccer Stats Hub is to make the reasoning transparent, not to eliminate the element of uncertainty.

outro: What really sets Soccer Stats Hub apart is not a louder tip. It's a completely transparent model with probabilities alongside the prices, tools for BTTS, Over 2.5, multi-builders, and match info you can actually go through pre-kick-off. With a premium subscription, you get all of this for well below the cost of most paid research you'll find out there.
Start free with a sample of today's board. Upgrade when you're ready to have the full range. Either way, expand a fixture and assess the reasoning for yourself.
